source_files: sobol_driver_v2.py (PARAM_NAMES, BASELINES, TIER2_AS_DOCUMENTED, TIER1_HALF_WIDTH, TIER2_HALF_WIDTH, make_bounds()) -- primary source, used unmodified by task1_full14.py
sobol_driver.py header comment -- original tiering rationale and the CV~0.144 figure
ml/robustness_audit.py PriorSpec list (lines 521-534) -- independent confirmation of the same 14 baselines and tier assignments
scenario_reported: as_documented (the evidentiary-tiering scenario; equal_width and tier1_promotion are deliberate perturbations of these same 14 baselines/tiers, not independent provenance)

gm2_synth.distribution_type_source: SALib problem dict passed to sobol_sample()/sobol_analyze() in sobol_driver_v2.py has no 'dists' key for any parameter -> SALib defaults every parameter to a uniform distribution over the given bounds; no log-uniform or other distribution is used anywhere in this project's Sobol pipeline.
gm2_synth.as_documented_bounds_note: These ARE the full support of the Uniform(lower, upper) prior used for sampling (i.e. equivalent to the 0th/100th percentile, not literally the 2.5th/97.5th of a distribution with tails beyond the bounds, since a uniform prior's support is bounded by construction). For reference, the empirical 2.5th/97.5th percentiles of this same Uniform(lower,upper) would be lower+0.025*(upper-lower) and lower+0.975*(upper-lower).
gm2_synth.relative_width_cv_note: CV = half_width/sqrt(3), the standard formula for a Uniform(base*(1-hw), base*(1+hw)) prior; hw=0.25 -> CV~0.1443 (Tier 1), hw=0.60 -> CV~0.3464 (Tier 2). The hw=0.25/CV~0.144 pairing is stated verbatim in this project's own sobol_driver.py comment.
gm2_synth.evidence_tier_source: sobol_driver_v2.py TIER2_AS_DOCUMENTED set (line 42) / ml/robustness_audit.py PriorSpec(...).tier assignments (lines 521-534) -- both agree exactly on which 5 of 14 params are Tier 2.
gm2_synth.source_count_note: Not recorded anywhere in the code/comments/docs as an explicit count.
